solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Love, Nablus exotic, mysterious, unlike this puzzle, one hopes!

definitions.text: mysterious, unlike this puzzle, one hopes!

indicators.note: exotic means strange and unfamiliar, so the letters of the two words are rearranged into a foreign shape

explanation.surface: A traveller finds love in the West Bank city of Nablus exotic and mysterious, and the setter hopes the puzzle is easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' shuffles LOVE and NABLUS together. The definition is 'mysterious', with the setter's joke that the puzzle, unlike the answer, can be cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious defies explanation; a puzzle nobody can crack is the setter's tongue-in-cheek fear.

clue.text: New country group, based on test ignoring India, seen as indifferent

indicators.note: in a down clue, the earlier pieces sit on top of the following one as a base

parts.note: the EU, the European Union, is a group of countries

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter for India is dropped from the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A new bloc of countries, having tested something, is seen as not taking sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops the I from TRIAL to leave TRAL; 'based on' stacks N and EU above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral party is indifferent in a dispute, favouring neither side; a synonym.

clue.text: Dislike arising from leader leaving speaking platform

indicators.note: the leader leaving means the platform word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: Hostility arises when a leader walks off the speaker's stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader leaving' removes the first letter P from PODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or strong dislike directed at someone; a synonym.

clue.text: In a picture, six upset America and supporter

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for America upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: US is America
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: Pictured: six people upsetting America and one of its backers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means turned upside down, so the two letters read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something visually is to present it as an image, by sight rather than words.

clue.text: Annual transfer of allotted space, we hear — Doris maybe kind of tense

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for allotted space is taken as spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a berth is a space allotted to a ship or a sleeper
Doris Day was an American singer and actress, so Day is one Doris
the present tense is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A grammar note about allotting space, Doris and verb tenses.
explanation.walkthrough: BERTH said aloud gives BIRTH. 'Annual transfer' is the cryptic definition: a gift handed over once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift given on someone's birthday each year is an annual handing over of a present.

clue.text: Feature writer, outspoken, supported by Liberal papers

indicators.note: outspoken signals that the writer's word is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: A frank feature writer is backed by Liberal newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: I said aloud gives EYE; 'supported by' puts L and ID beneath it in the down entry. 'Feature' means part of the face, not an article.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelid is one part of the face, and facial parts are called features.

clue.text: Fish limit getting around resistance

indicators.note: getting around means surrounding, so the limit word encloses the resistance symbol

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An angling rule about catch limits and getting around opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The carp is a freshwater fish often kept in ponds.

clue.text: Go at a clue in different way — making a list

indicators.note: doing the words in a different way means putting their letters in a different order

explanation.surface: Advice to a solver: attack a clue differently, perhaps by listing options.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a systematic list of items, such as goods for sale.

clue.text: Neglected animal track — sad

parts.note: a run is a track used by animals
feeling down means sad

explanation.surface: A sad, neglected path once used by animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-down building or area has been neglected and fallen into disrepair.

clue.text: Just starting, find useful Japanese index showing mountain name

indicators.note: just the starting letters means only the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to look a mountain up in a useful Japanese index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just starting' takes the first letters of find, useful, Japanese and index.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest peak, so Fuji is the name of a mountain.

clue.text: Cunning, pen in unusual entries

indicators.note: in means the pen goes inside the other letters
unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters of entries are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver writes with a pen in some odd-looking grid entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges entries into SERTINE, which then holds the pen; 'Cunning' is the snake-like sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine can mean sly or wily, like the snake in Eden; an adjectival sense.

clue.text: Something wrong with a peninsula

parts.note: a crime is a wrong act

explanation.surface: Something is amiss with a stretch of land surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimea is a peninsula jutting into the Black Sea.

clue.text: Legacy perhaps of dictator's attitude to come into view

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating aloud, so the attitude word is as spoken, a word with the same sound

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude
to loom is to come into view, often threateningly

explanation.surface: A tyrant's arrogant air is about to emerge as his legacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator's' means as said by someone dictating: AIR said aloud gives HEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a treasured object handed down the family, an example of something bequeathed.

clue.text: Vessels, modified, foil all threats initially

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters are reordered
initially means only the first letter of threats is used

explanation.surface: Ships, refitted, thwart every danger at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives T, which joins FOILALL as anagram fodder; 'modified' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats sailing together.

clue.text: Strange generation, losing love for fruit

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are jumbled
losing means the word gives up a letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: An odd generation that has lost its love of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing love' removes O from GENERATION, leaving GENERATIN; 'Strange' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Joke about northern group

indicators.note: about means around, so the joke word is wrapped around the letter for northern

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A joke about a band from the North.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a band of people associating together; a synonym.

clue.text: Device, electronic say, provides regular traveller with parking for month

indicators.note: parking for month means the letter for parking stands in place of the letter for month

parts.note: a commuter travels the same route regularly, to work and back
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: An electronic gadget gives the daily commuter a parking space for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the M in COMMUTER for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer is a machine that processes data, one example of an electronic device.

clue.text: Willing to consider musical work, European, on periphery

parts.note: OP, short for opus, labels a numbered musical work

indicators.note: the periphery of a word is its outside edge, so only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Open to an opera by a European on the fringes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on periphery' takes the outer letters of European, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open to an idea means being receptive and ready to entertain it.

clue.text: European note Conservative finds controversial

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
mi is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A European and a Conservative find a note contentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemic as an adjective describes argumentative, disputatious writing or speech.

clue.text: Attribute of required standard, extremely trusty

parts.note: proper means up to the correct standard

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of trusty are taken

explanation.surface: A quality meeting the right standard, utterly reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives TY, the ends of trusty.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is a quality or characteristic belonging to something.

clue.text: Have an impact, about right — one's garden feature

indicators.note: about means around, so the impact word surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: to tell is to have an effect, as in 'the strain began to tell'
one's is read as one is: I for one plus IS

explanation.surface: Making an impression in the right way is one's ornamental garden addition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes TRELL; 'one's' is read as 'one is', with I standing for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework in a garden for climbing plants.

clue.text: Pledge to include artist's style of music

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the pledge word wraps round the artist

parts.note: a gage is an old word for a pledge or thing left as security
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A promise to include an artist's musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: The pledge word is archaic, as in a gauntlet thrown down as a challenge; the artist is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a genre of electronic dance music, named after a New York club.

clue.text: Antagonise a learner — that is needless primarily, battle regularly lost

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
i.e., id est, means that is

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of needless counts
regularly lost means every other letter of battle is dropped

explanation.surface: Upsetting a novice is needless, and the battle is regularly lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly lost' drops B, T and L from battle, leaving ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to make them hostile or estranged; a synonym of turning them against you.

clue.text: Perhaps Mercury's scheme, out of this world?

definitions.note: read as 'perhaps Mercury is': the answer is what Mercury is

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
ET, the extraterrestrial, is from beyond our world

explanation.surface: The god Mercury's plan is fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury the messenger god misleads; here it is the planet nearest the Sun, and 'Mercury's' reads as 'Mercury is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the smallest body in the solar system orbiting the Sun as a planet, an example.

clue.text: A doctor with little hesitation identifying warning colour

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
er is a brief hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A doctor's brief hesitation spells out a warning sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber traffic lights warn drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Van meal bit off? Maybe yes, maybe no

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the food from the van slightly off? Hard to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ambivalent means having mixed feelings, unable to decide either way.

clue.text: Comfort from herbal medicine

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Relief from a herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm is a soothing ointment, and figuratively anything that gives comfort.

clue.text: Wizard entertaining millions — a high point

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the expert word contains the letter for millions

parts.note: an ace or wizard is an expert

explanation.surface: A magician amusing millions reaches a career peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the summit or peak of achievement.

clue.text: Compete, given award we're told for initiative

parts.note: to enter a contest is to compete

indicators.note: we're told signals the award word as heard, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: a prize is an award

explanation.surface: Taking part and winning a prize, we hear, shows drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise is resourcefulness and readiness to start new ventures.
